newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate climbs to 11 from 7.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate climbs to 11 from 7.8 pct.

text.p: A flurry of term loans on Wednesday pushed the Croatian average lending rate to 11.0 percent from 7.8 percent, dealers said.
Total settlements reached 40.5 million kuna ($6.1 million), down from Monday's 84.8 million as demand slackened on Zagreb's money market. Of this, fresh trade amounted to 32.5 million.
The interbank call money rate remained unchanged at 7.0 percent. Term rates varied between a steady 11 percent for one-month loans and 18 percent for a three-month loan.
Banks charged 16 percent for prolonged two-month borrowings.
The non-banking sector rolled over previous one-month funds at 9.0 and 15.0 percent.
The kuna mid-rate eased to 6.7265 from 6.6568 against the dollar and firmed slightly to 3.5609 versus the German mark. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 ($ = 6.654 Croatian Kuna)
